description.he: פורסם דוח הוועדה המיוחדת הבריטית בראשות סר וולטר שו, שחקרה את האלימות בפלשתינה באוגוסט 1929, והוא עורר מחלוקת מדינית שהובילה לחקירת הופ סימפסון.

sources.quote: THE Report* of the Special Commission, under the Chairmanship of Sir Walter Shaw, which was published in April, gave rise to acute controversy
a major outbreak of violence with unprecedented loss of life in 1929, which was investigated by the Shaw Commission.

notes.en: Published April 1930 per the October 1930 statement of policy; the exact day was not verified. The UN study calls the 1929 events a "Palestinian revolt"; naming of these events differs between accounts (covered by the conflicts layer).

name.en: Hope Simpson report and Passfield White Paper
name.ar: تقرير هوب سمبسون والكتاب الأبيض لباسفيلد
name.he: דוח הופ סימפסון והספר הלבן של פספילד

description.en: After Sir John Hope Simpson’s report on land settlement, immigration and development, the British government issued a statement of policy (Cmd. 3692) stressing a "double undertaking" to Jews and to the non-Jewish population and announcing tighter control of immigration and land transfers.
description.ar: بعد تقرير السير جون هوب سمبسون عن التوطين على الأراضي والهجرة والتنمية، أصدرت الحكومة البريطانية بيان سياسة (Cmd. 3692) يشدد على «التزام مزدوج» تجاه اليهود وتجاه السكان غير اليهود ويعلن تشديد الرقابة على الهجرة وانتقال الأراضي.
description.he: לאחר דוחו של סר ג׳ון הופ סימפסון על התיישבות בקרקע, הגירה ופיתוח, פרסמה ממשלת בריטניה הצהרת מדיניות (Cmd. 3692) המדגישה ״התחייבות כפולה״ ליהודים ולאוכלוסייה הלא־יהודית ומכריזה על החמרת הפיקוח על ההגירה ועל העברות קרקע.

sources.quote: Presented by the Secretary of State for the Colonies to Parliament by Command of His Majesty, October 1930
a double undertaking is involved, to the Jewish people on the one hand and to the non-Jewish population of Palestine on the other.

sources.locator: Part I, Passfield White Paper; quoting Chaim Weizmann
sources.quote: the most concerted effort – until the White Paper of 1939 – on the part of a British Government to retract the promise made to the Jewish people

notes.en: Named after Colonial Secretary Lord Passfield (Sidney Webb). The statement says it was framed after receipt of the Hope Simpson report. Zionist leaders, quoted in the UN study (Weizmann), saw it as a retreat from the Balfour Declaration; it was effectively reversed by the MacDonald letter of February 1931. Exact day of publication not verified (month precision).

name.en: MacDonald letter to Chaim Weizmann
name.ar: رسالة ماكدونالد إلى حاييم وايزمان
name.he: מכתב מקדונלד לחיים ויצמן

description.en: British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald wrote to Zionist leader Chaim Weizmann "to remove certain misconceptions" about the 1930 White Paper, stating that the Mandate was an undertaking to the Jewish people as a whole; the letter was published in Hansard the same day.
description.ar: كتب رئيس الوزراء البريطاني رمزي ماكدونالد إلى الزعيم الصهيوني حاييم وايزمان «لإزالة بعض المفاهيم الخاطئة» بشأن الكتاب الأبيض لسنة 1930، مؤكداً أن الانتداب التزام تجاه الشعب اليهودي ككل؛ ونُشرت الرسالة في هانسارد في اليوم نفسه.
description.he: ראש ממשלת בריטניה ראמזי מקדונלד כתב למנהיג הציוני חיים ויצמן ״כדי להסיר אי־הבנות מסוימות״ בנוגע לספר הלבן של 1930, וקבע שהמנדט הוא התחייבות כלפי העם היהודי כולו; המכתב פורסם בהנסרד באותו יום.

sources.quote: the undertaking of the Mandate is an undertaking to the Jewish people and not only to the Jewish population of Palestine
The “MacDonald letter” made clear that Palestine would be governed in accordance with the Churchill policy of 1922

notes.en: Dated 10 Downing Street, 13 February 1931. The UN study states that the restrictions suggested by Lord Passfield on Jewish immigration and land transfers were thereby not applied; it quotes Weizmann describing the Passfield policy as an attack that was "successfully repulsed".

name.en: Second British census of Palestine
name.ar: الإحصاء البريطاني الثاني لفلسطين
name.he: המפקד הבריטי השני בפלשתינה

description.en: The Mandate government took its second census of Palestine at midnight on 18 November 1931, a more systematic operation than that of 1922.
description.ar: أجرت حكومة الانتداب إحصاءها الثاني لفلسطين عند منتصف ليل 18 تشرين الثاني/نوفمبر 1931، وكان أكثر منهجية من إحصاء 1922.
description.he: ממשלת המנדט ערכה את המפקד השני שלה בפלשתינה בחצות ליל 18 בנובמבר 1931, מבצע שיטתי יותר מזה של 1922.

sources.quote: census of Palestine taken at midnight on the 18th of November 1931
The 1931 census was a more scientific operation.

notes.en: Superintendent of the census: E. Mills. Results are handled in the population layer.

name.en: Arab Higher Committee formed
name.ar: تشكيل اللجنة العربية العليا
name.he: הקמת הוועד הערבי העליון

description.en: Palestinian Arab political parties formed the Arab Higher Committee, chaired by the Mufti of Jerusalem, Hajj Amin al-Husseini, to coordinate a nationwide general strike.
description.ar: شكّلت الأحزاب السياسية العربية الفلسطينية اللجنة العربية العليا، برئاسة مفتي القدس الحاج أمين الحسيني، لتنسيق إضراب عام على مستوى البلاد.
description.he: מפלגות פוליטיות ערביות פלסטיניות הקימו את הוועד הערבי העליון, בראשות מופתי ירושלים חאג׳ אמין אל־חוסייני, כדי לתאם שביתה כללית ארצית.

sources.quote: on 25 April the Arab Higher Committee (AHC) was formed, chaired by Haj Amin al-Husseini, to coordinate and support a nationwide general strike
A new union of Palestinian political parties was formed, the Arab Higher Committee, headed by the Mufti of Jerusalem, Al Hajj Amin al-Husseini.

notes.en: The general strike began on 8 May 1936 (palquest). The UN study records that the Mandate authorities later proscribed the committee and deported several leaders after the 1937 renewal of violence. The revolt itself belongs to the conflicts layer.

name.en: Peel Commission report recommends partition
name.ar: تقرير لجنة بيل يوصي بالتقسيم
name.he: דוח ועדת פיל ממליץ על חלוקה

description.en: The Palestine Royal Commission (Peel Commission) published its report, the first official British proposal to partition Palestine into a Jewish state and an Arab state, with Jerusalem, Bethlehem, Nazareth and a corridor to Jaffa remaining under a British mandate.
description.ar: نشرت اللجنة الملكية لفلسطين (لجنة بيل) تقريرها، وهو أول اقتراح بريطاني رسمي لتقسيم فلسطين إلى دولة يهودية ودولة عربية، على أن تبقى القدس وبيت لحم والناصرة وممر إلى يافا تحت انتداب بريطاني.
description.he: ועדת המלוכה לפלשתינה (ועדת פיל) פרסמה את דוחה, ההצעה הבריטית הרשמית הראשונה לחלק את פלשתינה למדינה יהודית ולמדינה ערבית, כאשר ירושלים, בית לחם, נצרת ומסדרון ליפו נשארות תחת מנדט בריטי.

sources.quote: The final report was published on July 7, 1937.
the commission recommended the partition of Palestine into two states, one Jewish and one Arab.
an elaboration of the Statement of Policy issued by the British Government on July 7, last
Jerusalem, Bethlehem and Nazareth, with a corridor to the sea at Jaffa, would continue under a British Mandate

notes.en: Report published (Cmd. 5479) together with a government statement of policy on 7 July 1937. Reactions differed: according to palquest (Parsons) the Zionist leadership accepted the principle of partition but not the proposed map, while the Palestinian leadership condemned the partition recommendation; the report also proposed transferring Arab inhabitants out of the proposed Jewish state. The plan was not implemented (see Woodhead Commission, 1938). Published in London.

name.en: Woodhead Commission report; Britain drops partition
name.ar: تقرير لجنة وودهيد؛ بريطانيا تتخلى عن التقسيم
name.he: דוח ועדת וודהד; בריטניה זונחת את החלוקה

description.en: The British government published the Palestine Partition (Woodhead) Commission report together with a statement concluding that the creation of separate Arab and Jewish states was impracticable, and proposed a London conference with Arab and Jewish representatives.
description.ar: نشرت الحكومة البريطانية تقرير لجنة تقسيم فلسطين (لجنة وودهيد) مع بيان خلصت فيه إلى أن إقامة دولتين عربية ويهودية منفصلتين غير عملية، واقترحت عقد مؤتمر في لندن مع ممثلين عن العرب واليهود.
description.he: ממשלת בריטניה פרסמה את דוח ועדת החלוקה של פלשתינה (ועדת וודהד) יחד עם הצהרה המסיקה שהקמת מדינות ערבית ויהודית נפרדות אינה מעשית, והציעה כינוס ועידה בלונדון עם נציגים ערבים ויהודים.

sources.quote: In the Statement on Palestine, issued on 9th November, 1938, His Majesty's Government announced their intention to invite representatives of the Arabs of Palestine

the political, administrative and financial difficulties involved in the proposal to create independent Arab and Jewish states inside Palestine is so great that such a solution of the problem is impracticable
this solution of the problem is impracticable
This Commission, which held its inquiries in Palestine from April to August 1938, concluded that the Royal Commission’s plan was unworkable

notes.en: The report (Cmd. 5854) is dated October 1938 and the statement (Cmd. 5893) November 1938; both were made public on 9 November 1938 (Cmd. 6019; US State Department press release of the same day). The London talks it proposed preceded the May 1939 White Paper (Cmd. 6019, opening paragraph).

name.en: British White Paper of 1939
name.ar: الكتاب الأبيض البريطاني لسنة 1939
name.he: הספר הלבן הבריטי של 1939

description.en: Britain’s statement of policy (Cmd. 6019) envisaged an independent Palestine State within ten years shared by Arabs and Jews, limited Jewish immigration to 75,000 over five years (further immigration subject to Arab consent) and restricted land transfers.
description.ar: تصوّر بيان السياسة البريطانية (Cmd. 6019) دولة فلسطين مستقلة خلال عشر سنوات يتشارك فيها العرب واليهود، وحدّ الهجرة اليهودية بـ75,000 شخص على مدى خمس سنوات (وما بعدها رهن بموافقة العرب)، وقيّد انتقال الأراضي.
description.he: הצהרת המדיניות הבריטית (Cmd. 6019) שאפה למדינת פלשתינה עצמאית בתוך עשר שנים, משותפת לערבים וליהודים, הגבילה את ההגירה היהודית ל־75,000 לחמש שנים (המשך הגירה מותנה בהסכמת הערבים) והגבילה העברות קרקע.

sources.quote: The objective of His Majesty's Government is the establishment within 10 years of an independent Palestine State
Presented by the Secretary of State for the Colonies to Parliament by Command of His Majesty May, 1939
Zionists condemned the new policy, accusing Britain of favoring the Arabs.

sources.locator: Colonial Secretary's speech quoting the Jewish Agency statement
sources.quote: transfer authority over Palestine to a present Arab majority and put the Jewish population at the mercy of that majority
though not formally accepted by the most influential Arab leaders, the 1939 White Paper's restrictions on Jewish immigration and land settlement were plainly designed to protect Arab rights
A new White Paper was issued in May 1939, disclaiming any intention to create a Jewish State, rejecting Arab demands that Palestine become independent as an Arab State

notes.en: Commonly dated 17 May 1939; the sources opened give only "May 1939", so month precision is used (Hansard shows the Commons debate on 22-23 May 1939). Jewish Agency and Zionist reaction was strongly negative (Hansard, Britannica); per UNSCOP the leading Arab leaders did not formally accept it either. The League’s Permanent Mandates Commission expressed reservations (UN study). Issued in London.

name.en: Biltmore Program
name.ar: برنامج بالتيمور
name.he: תוכנית בילטמור

description.en: A Zionist conference held in New York publicly adopted the aim of establishing Palestine as a Jewish commonwealth and rejected the 1939 White Paper.
description.ar: تبنى مؤتمر صهيوني عُقد في نيويورك علناً هدف إقامة فلسطين كومنولثاً يهودياً ورفض الكتاب الأبيض لسنة 1939.
description.he: ועידה ציונית שהתכנסה בניו יורק אימצה בפומבי את המטרה להקים את פלשתינה כקהילייה יהודית (קומונוולת׳) ודחתה את הספר הלבן של 1939.

sources.quote: In May 1942 the Jewish Agency Executive, meeting in New York, formally made public in what is known as the “Biltmore Programme”
The Conference affirms its unalterable rejection of the White Paper of May 1939 and denies its moral or legal validity.

notes.en: Named after the Biltmore Hotel in New York. Single source (UN committee study, which frames it as a programme for "a Jewish State in Palestine through unlimited immigration"); exact days not verified.

name.en: League of Arab States founded
name.ar: تأسيس جامعة الدول العربية
name.he: הקמת הליגה הערבית

description.en: Egypt, Iraq, Lebanon, Saudi Arabia, Syria, Transjordan and Yemen signed the Pact of the League of Arab States in Cairo, which became the League’s permanent seat.
description.ar: وقّعت مصر والعراق ولبنان والسعودية وسوريا وشرق الأردن واليمن ميثاق جامعة الدول العربية في القاهرة، التي أصبحت المقر الدائم للجامعة.
description.he: מצרים, עיראק, לבנון, ערב הסעודית, סוריה, עבר הירדן ותימן חתמו בקהיר על אמנת הליגה הערבית, וקהיר הפכה למושבה הקבוע.

sources.quote: The present Pact has been drawn up in the Arabic language in Cairo and dated 8 Rabi al Thani 1364 (March 22, 1945)
The permanent seat of the League of Arab States shall be Cairo.
formed in Cairo on March 22, 1945, as an outgrowth of Pan-Arabism

notes.en: Founding states as listed in the Pact’s preamble (Avalon). The Pact’s Annex on Palestine affirms that Palestine became independent in principle when separated from the Ottoman Empire.

name.en: Anglo-American Committee of Inquiry report
name.ar: تقرير لجنة التحقيق الأنجلو - أمريكية
name.he: דוח הוועדה האנגלו־אמריקנית לחקירה

description.en: A joint British-American committee reported from Lausanne, recommending among other things the immediate authorisation of 100,000 immigration certificates for Jewish survivors of Nazi persecution, that Palestine be "neither a Jewish state nor an Arab state", and that early independence be deferred.
description.ar: قدمت لجنة بريطانية - أمريكية مشتركة تقريرها من لوزان، موصيةً من جملة أمور بالإذن الفوري بمئة ألف شهادة هجرة للناجين اليهود من الاضطهاد النازي، وبأن تكون فلسطين «لا دولة يهودية ولا دولة عربية»، وبتأجيل الاستقلال المبكر.
description.he: ועדה משותפת בריטית־אמריקנית דיווחה מלוזאן והמליצה, בין השאר, על מתן אישור מיידי ל־100,000 רישיונות הגירה לניצולי רדיפות הנאצים היהודים, על כך שפלשתינה תהיה ״לא מדינה יהודית ולא מדינה ערבית״ ועל דחיית העצמאות המוקדמת.

sources.quote: Report to the United States Government and His Majesty’s Government in the United Kingdom Lausanne, Switzerland, April 20, 1946
that 100,000 certificates be authorized immediately for the admission into Palestine of Jews who have been the victims of Nazi and Fascist persecution
That Palestine shall be neither a Jewish state nor an Arab state.
British Foreign Secretary Ernest Bevin announced the formation of the AACI, consisting of six British and six US investigators, on 13 November 1945.

notes.en: The committee sat in Washington, London, Europe, Cairo and Palestine before concluding in Switzerland (preface; appendix I). Palquest (Allen) notes that the follow-up Morrison-Grady provincial autonomy plan was rejected by Truman and the Zionists and by the Arabs, who saw it as laying the basis for partition.

name.en: UN Special Committee on Palestine (UNSCOP) established and reports
name.ar: تشكيل لجنة الأمم المتحدة الخاصة بفلسطين (أنسكوب) وتقريرها
name.he: הקמת ועדת האו״ם המיוחדת לפלשתינה (אונסקופ) ודוחה

description.en: A special session of the UN General Assembly created an eleven-member Special Committee on Palestine, which investigated in Palestine and the region and signed its report on 31 August 1947 (majority plan: partition with economic union; minority plan: a federal state).
description.ar: أنشأت دورة خاصة للجمعية العامة للأمم المتحدة لجنة خاصة بفلسطين من أحد عشر عضواً، حققت في فلسطين والمنطقة ووقّعت تقريرها في 31 آب/أغسطس 1947 (خطة الأغلبية: التقسيم مع اتحاد اقتصادي؛ وخطة الأقلية: دولة اتحادية).
description.he: מושב מיוחד של העצרת הכללית של האו״ם הקים ועדה מיוחדת לפלשתינה בת אחד עשר חברים, שחקרה בפלשתינה ובאזור וחתמה על דוחה ב־31 באוגוסט 1947 (תוכנית הרוב: חלוקה עם איחוד כלכלי; תוכנית המיעוט: מדינה פדרלית).

sources.locator: resolution 106 (S-1), para. 1 (PDF/OCR text; quote normalised for OCR, hyphenation and ligature errors)
sources.quote: A Special Committee be created for the above-mentioned purpose consisting of the representatives of Australia, Canada, Czechoslovakia, Guatemala, India, Iran, Netherlands, Peru, Sweden, Uruguay and Yugoslavia

sources.locator: closing formula (PDF/OCR text; quote normalised for OCR, hyphenation and ligature errors)
sources.quote: Seventy-ninth plenary meeting, 15 May 1947.
From that date until 31 August 1947, the day of the signing of this report, the Special Committee held sixteen public meetings and thirty-six private meetings.
The majority proposal: Partition with economic union

sources.locator: Part II, section on UNSCOP (minority plan)
sources.quote: Jerusalem, which shall be the capital of the independent federal State of Palestine

notes.en: The committee first met at the UN’s interim headquarters at Lake Success, New York, on 26 May 1947 and worked in Jerusalem, Beirut and Geneva (A/364). The Arab Higher Committee did not cooperate with it (A/364, Chapter I section c). End date = signing of the report.

name.en: UN General Assembly Resolution 181 (Partition Plan)
name.ar: قرار الجمعية العامة للأمم المتحدة 181 (خطة التقسيم)
name.he: החלטת העצרת הכללית של האו״ם 181 (תוכנית החלוקה)

description.en: The UN General Assembly adopted, by 33 votes to 13 with 10 abstentions, a plan to end the Mandate and partition Palestine into independent Arab and Jewish states with economic union and a special international regime for Jerusalem.
description.ar: اعتمدت الجمعية العامة للأمم المتحدة بأغلبية 33 صوتاً مقابل 13 وامتناع 10 عن التصويت خطةً لإنهاء الانتداب وتقسيم فلسطين إلى دولتين عربية ويهودية مستقلتين مع اتحاد اقتصادي ونظام دولي خاص للقدس.
description.he: העצרת הכללית של האו״ם אימצה, ברוב של 33 קולות נגד 13 ועשרה נמנעים, תוכנית לסיום המנדט ולחלוקת פלשתינה למדינות ערבית ויהודית עצמאיות עם איחוד כלכלי ומשטר בין־לאומי מיוחד לירושלים.

sources.locator: closing formula (PDF/OCR text; quote normalised for OCR, hyphenation and ligature errors)
sources.quote: Hundred and twenty-eighth plenary meeting, 29 November 1947.
Independent Arab and Jewish States and the Special International Regime for the City of Jerusalem, set forth in Part III of this Plan, shall come into existence in Palestine
In favour: 33
This recognition by the United Nations of the right of the Jewish people to establish their State is irrevocable.
the plan proposed a Jewish state on more than half of Mandate Palestine at a time when Jews comprised less than a third of the population and owned less than 7 percent of the land

notes.en: Votes: 33 in favour, 13 against (including Egypt, Iraq, Lebanon, Saudi Arabia, Syria and Yemen), 10 abstentions (Avalon vote list). Israel’s Declaration of Independence cites it as irrevocable UN recognition of the Jewish people’s right to a state; palquest (Winder) notes it passed "in the face of strong Arab opposition" and argues it allotted the larger share of the land to the Jewish minority. The UN then had its interim headquarters at Lake Success, New York; coordinates are those of New York City (approximate).

name.en: End of the British Mandate; Declaration of the Establishment of the State of Israel
name.ar: نهاية الانتداب البريطاني؛ إعلان قيام دولة إسرائيل
name.he: סיום המנדט הבריטי; הכרזה על הקמת מדינת ישראל

description.en: On the day the British Mandate ended, the Jewish People’s Council meeting in Tel Aviv proclaimed the State of Israel, effective from the Mandate’s termination at midnight on 14/15 May 1948; the United States recognised it the same day.
description.ar: في اليوم الذي انتهى فيه الانتداب البريطاني، أعلن مجلس الشعب اليهودي المجتمع في تل أبيب قيام دولة إسرائيل، سارياً من انتهاء الانتداب عند منتصف ليل 14/15 أيار/مايو 1948؛ واعترفت بها الولايات المتحدة في اليوم نفسه.
description.he: ביום שבו הסתיים המנדט הבריטי הכריזה מועצת העם היהודי, שהתכנסה בתל אביב, על הקמת מדינת ישראל, בתוקף מסיום המנדט בחצות 14/15 במאי 1948; ארצות הברית הכירה בה באותו יום.

sources.quote: HEREBY DECLARE THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A JEWISH STATE IN ERETZ-ISRAEL, TO BE KNOWN AS THE STATE OF ISRAEL.
with effect from the moment of the termination of the Mandate being tonight, the eve of Sabbath, the 6th Iyar, 5708 (15th May, 1948)
On May 14, 1948, David Ben-Gurion, the head of the Jewish Agency, proclaimed the establishment of the State of Israel.
the declaration cherry-picked from this resolution only what granted international legitimacy
Every 15 May since 1948, Palestinians, wherever they are gathered in the homeland or the diaspora, commemorate the anniversary of the disaster that befell them as a people.

notes.en: Facts agreed; meaning contested. In Israel the date is Independence Day (5 Iyar); the declaration appeals to the Arab inhabitants to participate "on the basis of full and equal citizenship" (Avalon). Palestinians mark 15 May as Nakba Day, commemorating the displacement of 1947-49 (palquest Charif; UN "About the Nakba"); palquest (Nabulsi) criticises the declaration for citing only the Jewish-state half of Resolution 181.

name.en: Constantin Zureiq publishes "The Meaning of the Nakba"
name.ar: قسطنطين زريق ينشر «معنى النكبة»
name.he: קונסטנטין זריק מפרסם את ״משמעות הנכבה״

description.en: Syrian historian Constantin Zureiq (Zurayk) published Maʿna al-Nakba ("The Meaning of the Catastrophe"), which introduced "Nakba" as the term for the Arab defeat and Palestinian catastrophe of 1948.
description.ar: نشر المؤرخ السوري قسطنطين زريق «معنى النكبة»، الذي أدخل «النكبة» مصطلحاً لهزيمة العرب وكارثة الفلسطينيين سنة 1948.
description.he: ההיסטוריון הסורי קונסטנטין זריק (זוריק) פרסם את ״معنى النكبة״ (״משמעות האסון״), שהכניס את ״הנכבה״ כמונח להפסד הערבי ולאסון הפלסטיני של 1948.

sources.quote: In his book The Meaning of the Nakba (Ma‘na al-Nakba), published in August 1948, Constantine Zurayk argued that the effects of the Nakba could be overcome in two closely connected ways.
Zurayk described the Nakba as the catastrophic failure by the Arabs to stop the establishment of the State of Israel
The Nakba, which means “catastrophe” in Arabic, refers to the mass displacement and dispossession of Palestinians during the 1948 Arab-Israeli war.

notes.en: Publication month agreed (August 1948). Interpretation differs: palquest (Charif) presents Zurayk’s book as a call for cultural renewal and Arab nation-building after the catastrophe, and treats the Nakba as the expulsion and dispossession of Palestinians; pro-Israel commentators (e.g. Stein, Jewish Chronicle 2024) stress that Zurayk blamed Arab states’ failure rather than Israel. The UN today uses the term for the displacement and dispossession of Palestinians in 1948. Official PA inauguration of Nakba Day in 1998 is outside this file’s period and was not verified here. Place of publication (Beirut) not confirmed in the sources opened.

name.en: All-Palestine Government and Gaza declaration of independence
name.ar: حكومة عموم فلسطين وإعلان الاستقلال في غزة
name.he: ממשלת כל־פלשתין והכרזת העצמאות בעזה

description.en: After the Arab League announced an All-Palestine Government seated in Gaza (20 September 1948), a Palestine National Council convened in Gaza under the Mufti of Jerusalem passed resolutions culminating in a declaration of independence over the whole of Palestine.
description.ar: بعد أن أعلنت جامعة الدول العربية حكومة عموم فلسطين ومقرها غزة (20 أيلول/سبتمبر 1948)، عقد مجلس وطني فلسطيني في غزة برئاسة مفتي القدس وأصدر قرارات توّجها بإعلان استقلال شامل لكل فلسطين.
description.he: לאחר שהליגה הערבית הכריזה על ממשלת כל־פלשתין שמושבה בעזה (20 בספטמבר 1948), התכנסה בעזה מועצה לאומית פלסטינית בראשות מופתי ירושלים ואימצה החלטות שהגיעו לשיאן בהכרזת עצמאות על פני כל פלשתינה.

sources.quote: The formal announcement of the Arab League's decision to form the Government of All-Palestine was issued on 20 September.
a Palestinian National Council was convened in Gaza on 30 September 1948, under the chairmanship of the Mufti of Jerusalem
a Palestine National Council which met in Gaza in 1October 1948, which was the first Palestinian legislative authority

notes.en: Sources differ by a day: Shlaim gives 30 September for the council’s convening, the Palestinian National Council website 1 October 1948 (end date). The government, headed by Ahmad Hilmi Abd al-Baqi, soon moved to Cairo; Shlaim judges it "an Egyptian-led phantom" created partly to counter Transjordan’s claims, while the PNC presents the 1948 council as the first Palestinian legislative authority. The Jericho Congress (1 December 1948) repudiated it.

name.en: Jericho Congress calls for union with Transjordan
name.ar: مؤتمر أريحا يدعو إلى الوحدة مع شرق الأردن
name.he: ועידת יריחו קוראת לאיחוד עם עבר הירדן

description.en: A congress of Palestinian notables convened at Jericho under King Abdullah’s sponsorship asked for unity of Arab Palestine with Transjordan and proclaimed Abdullah king of all Palestine.
description.ar: طلب مؤتمر لوجهاء فلسطينيين عُقد في أريحا برعاية الملك عبد الله وحدة فلسطين العربية مع شرق الأردن وبايع عبد الله ملكاً على كل فلسطين.
description.he: ועידה של נכבדים פלסטינים שהתכנסה ביריחו בחסות המלך עבדאללה ביקשה איחוד של פלשתינה הערבית עם עבר הירדן והכריזה על עבדאללה כמלך כל פלשתינה.

sources.quote: Held in Jericho on 1 December 1948, the Jericho Congress was convened in response to the establishment of the State of Israel
The conferees voted unanimously to request unity with Jordan; proclaimed Abdullah I ibn Hussein to be king of all Palestine

notes.en: Presided over by Shaykh Muhammad Ali Jaʿbari, mayor of Hebron. The Jordanian cabinet approved its resolutions on 7 December and parliament ratified them on 13 December 1948 (Tutunji); it also repudiated the All-Palestine Government in Gaza. Egypt opposed the union. Formal union followed on 24 April 1950.

name.en: UN General Assembly Resolution 194 (III)
name.ar: قرار الجمعية العامة للأمم المتحدة 194 (د-3)
name.he: החלטת העצרת הכללית של האו״ם 194 (III)

description.en: The UN General Assembly established a Conciliation Commission for Palestine, called for an international regime for Jerusalem, and resolved that refugees wishing to return home and live at peace should be permitted to do so, with compensation for those choosing not to return.
description.ar: أنشأت الجمعية العامة للأمم المتحدة لجنة توفيق خاصة بفلسطين، ودعت إلى نظام دولي للقدس، وقررت وجوب السماح للاجئين الراغبين في العودة إلى ديارهم والعيش بسلام بذلك، مع تعويض من يختارون عدم العودة.
description.he: העצרת הכללית של האו״ם הקימה ועדת פיוס לפלשתינה, קראה למשטר בין־לאומי בירושלים והחליטה שיש לאפשר לפליטים הרוצים לשוב לבתיהם ולחיות בשלום לעשות זאת, עם פיצוי למי שבוחרים שלא לשוב.

sources.quote: Resolves that the refugees wishing to return to their homes and live at peace with their neighbours should be permitted to do so at the earliest practicable date
Hundred and eighty-sixth plenary meeting, 11 December 1948.
The Commission’s efforts to link the two questions were unsuccessful.

symbolized the international commitment to implement UN General Assembly Resolution 194, which resolves in paragraph 11 that the refugees return to their homes or resettle elsewhere with compensation.

notes.en: Text and date agreed; the meaning of paragraph 11 is contested. Palestinian accounts and UN bodies treat it as the basis of a right of return (palquest; the UN study notes the call has been reiterated annually by the General Assembly). The UN study records that the Arab states initially voted against the resolution, and that at Lausanne (1949) Israel insisted the refugee question be linked to a territorial settlement in a peace treaty while the Arab states wanted it settled first. An Israeli official text on paragraph 11 was not opened for this record.

name.en: Egyptian-Israeli General Armistice Agreement
name.ar: اتفاقية الهدنة العامة المصرية - الإسرائيلية
name.he: הסכם שביתת הנשק הכללי בין מצרים לישראל

description.en: Egypt and Israel signed a general armistice agreement at Rhodes under UN mediation, leaving the Gaza Strip area under Egyptian control.
description.ar: وقّعت مصر وإسرائيل اتفاقية هدنة عامة في رودس بوساطة الأمم المتحدة، تاركةً منطقة قطاع غزة تحت السيطرة المصرية.
description.he: מצרים וישראל חתמו ברודוס על הסכם שביתת נשק כללי בתיווך האו״ם, שהותיר את אזור רצועת עזה בשליטה מצרית.

sources.quote: DONE at Rhodes, Island of Rhodes, Greece, on the twenty-fourth of February nineteen forty-nine.
armistice agreements between Israel on the one hand and Egypt, Jordan, Lebanon and Syria on the other, which were signed between February and July 1949

notes.en: Negotiated under UN Acting Mediator Ralph Bunche (UN study). Rhodes coordinates are those of the island (approximate).

name.en: Lebanese-Israeli General Armistice Agreement
name.ar: اتفاقية الهدنة العامة اللبنانية - الإسرائيلية
name.he: הסכם שביתת הנשק הכללי בין לבנון לישראל

description.en: Lebanon and Israel signed a general armistice agreement at Ras en-Naqoura on the border.
description.ar: وقّعت لبنان وإسرائيل اتفاقية هدنة عامة في رأس الناقورة على الحدود.
description.he: לבנון וישראל חתמו בראס א־נאקורה שעל הגבול על הסכם שביתת נשק כללי.

sources.locator: signature clause (PDF/OCR text; quote normalised for OCR, hyphenation and ligature errors)
sources.quote: DONE at Ras En Naqoura on the twenty-third of March nineteen forty-nine
armistice agreements between Israel on the one hand and Egypt, Jordan, Lebanon and Syria on the other, which were signed between February and July 1949

notes.en: Signed in the presence of the personal deputy of the UN Acting Mediator.

name.en: Jordanian-Israeli General Armistice Agreement
name.ar: اتفاقية الهدنة العامة الأردنية - الإسرائيلية
name.he: הסכם שביתת הנשק הכללי בין ירדן לישראל

description.en: Jordan and Israel signed a general armistice agreement at Rhodes whose armistice line left the West Bank and East Jerusalem under Jordanian control.
description.ar: وقّعت الأردن وإسرائيل اتفاقية هدنة عامة في رودس تركت خط هدنتها الضفة الغربية والقدس الشرقية تحت السيطرة الأردنية.
description.he: ירדן וישראל חתמו ברודוס על הסכם שביתת נשק כללי שקו שביתת הנשק שלו הותיר את הגדה המערבית ואת מזרח ירושלים בשליטה ירדנית.

sources.quote: DONE at Rhodes, Island of Rhodes, Greece, on the third of April one thousand nine hundred and forty-nine

sources.locator: covering cablegram (PDF/OCR text; quote normalised for OCR, hyphenation and ligature errors)
sources.quote: Rhodes, 3 April 1949

sources.locator: statement of 27 April 1950 (Hansard column marker 1138 omitted from quote)
sources.quote: The existing boundary is the line laid down in the Armistice Agreement signed between Israel and Jordan on 3rd April, 1949

notes.en: The UK (Hansard 1950) treated the armistice line as the boundary pending a final settlement. Rhodes coordinates are those of the island (approximate).

name.en: Israel admitted to the United Nations
name.ar: قبول إسرائيل في عضوية الأمم المتحدة
name.he: ישראל מתקבלת לאומות המאוחדות

description.en: The UN General Assembly, on the Security Council’s recommendation, admitted Israel as a member state, recalling its resolutions of 29 November 1947 and 11 December 1948 and Israel’s declarations on their implementation.
description.ar: قبلت الجمعية العامة للأمم المتحدة، بناءً على توصية مجلس الأمن، إسرائيل دولةً عضواً، مذكّرةً بقراريها المؤرخين 29 تشرين الثاني/نوفمبر 1947 و11 كانون الأول/ديسمبر 1948 وبتصريحات إسرائيل بشأن تنفيذهما.
description.he: העצרת הכללית של האו״ם, לפי המלצת מועצת הביטחון, קיבלה את ישראל כמדינה חברה, תוך הזכרת החלטותיה מ־29 בנובמבר 1947 ומ־11 בדצמבר 1948 והצהרות ישראל בדבר יישומן.

sources.locator: operative para. 2 (PDF/OCR text; quote normalised for OCR, hyphenation and ligature errors)
sources.quote: Decides to admit Israel to membership in the United Nations.

sources.locator: closing formula (PDF/OCR text; quote normalised for OCR, hyphenation and ligature errors)
sources.quote: Two hundred and seventh plenary meeting, 11 May 1949.

sources.locator: preamble (PDF/OCR text; quote normalised for OCR, hyphenation and ligature errors)
sources.quote: Recalling its resolutions of 29 November 1947 and 11 December 1948 and taking note of the declarations and explanations made by the representative of the Government of Israel

notes.en: Resolution 273 (III). The preambular reference to resolutions 181 and 194 is often cited in later debates over Israel’s obligations; that debate is not summarised here. Venue: UN General Assembly, New York area (coordinates of New York City, approximate).

name.en: Lausanne Protocol (UN Conciliation Commission)
name.ar: بروتوكول لوزان (لجنة التوفيق التابعة للأمم المتحدة)
name.he: פרוטוקול לוזאן (ועדת הפיוס של האו״ם)

description.en: At the Lausanne conference of the UN Conciliation Commission for Palestine, Israel and the Arab states signed separate protocols accepting the partition-plan map as a basis for discussions; the talks ended without agreement.
description.ar: في مؤتمر لوزان للجنة التوفيق التابعة للأمم المتحدة بشأن فلسطين، وقّعت إسرائيل والدول العربية بروتوكولات منفصلة تقبل خريطة خطة التقسيم أساساً للمباحثات؛ وانتهت المحادثات دون اتفاق.
description.he: בוועידת לוזאן של ועדת הפיוס של האו״ם לפלשתינה חתמו ישראל והמדינות הערביות על פרוטוקולים נפרדים שקיבלו את מפת תוכנית החלוקה כבסיס לדיונים; השיחות הסתיימו ללא הסכמה.

sources.locator: Part II, "The Conciliation Commission and the Lausanne protocols"
sources.quote: On 12 May 1949, two separate protocols were signed by the Arab States and Israel, agreeing to use the partition resolution’s boundaries as a “basis for discussions with the Commission”.
The Commission was able to arrange a conference in Lausanne in April 1949, consisting of separate talks with the two sides

notes.en: Single source (UN committee study). The Commission’s later conference in Paris (1951) was also inconclusive.

name.en: Israeli-Syrian General Armistice Agreement
name.ar: اتفاقية الهدنة العامة السورية - الإسرائيلية
name.he: הסכם שביתת הנשק הכללי בין סוריה לישראל

description.en: Syria and Israel signed the last of the 1949 general armistice agreements, at Hill 232 near Mahanayim.
description.ar: وقّعت سوريا وإسرائيل آخر اتفاقيات الهدنة العامة لسنة 1949، عند التلة 232 قرب محنايم.
description.he: סוריה וישראל חתמו על האחרון מבין הסכמי שביתת הנשק הכלליים של 1949, בגבעה 232 ליד מחניים.

sources.locator: signature clause (PDF/OCR text; quote normalised for OCR, hyphenation and ligature errors)
sources.quote: DONE at Hill 232 near Mahanayim on the twentieth of July nineteen forty-nine
armistice agreements between Israel on the one hand and Egypt, Jordan, Lebanon and Syria on the other, which were signed between February and July 1949

notes.en: Lines and zones defined by the agreement belong to the territories layer. Coordinates are those of Kibbutz Mahanayim (approximate for Hill 232).

name.en: UNRWA established
name.ar: تأسيس الأونروا
name.he: הקמת אונר״א

description.en: The UN General Assembly established the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA) to carry out relief and works programmes for Palestine refugees.
description.ar: أنشأت الجمعية العامة للأمم المتحدة وكالة الأمم المتحدة لإغاثة وتشغيل اللاجئين الفلسطينيين في الشرق الأدنى (الأونروا) لتنفيذ برامج الإغاثة والأشغال للاجئين الفلسطينيين.
description.he: העצרת הכללית של האו״ם הקימה את סוכנות הסעד והתעסוקה של האו״ם לפליטי פלסטין במזרח הקרוב (אונר״א) כדי לבצע תוכניות סעד ותעסוקה לפליטים פלסטינים.

sources.locator: para. 7 (PDF/OCR text; quote normalised for OCR, hyphenation and ligature errors)
sources.quote: Establishes the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East

sources.locator: closing formula (PDF/OCR text; quote normalised for OCR, hyphenation and ligature errors)
sources.quote: 273rd plenary meeting, 8 December 1949.
it remains a temporary body whose mandate has been regularly renewed since 1950 for periods lasting from three to five years.

notes.en: Resolution 302 (IV) provided for the transfer of the assets of the earlier UN Relief for Palestine Refugees to UNRWA by 1 April 1950 (para. 12); the date on which UNRWA began field operations was not verified in the sources opened.

name.en: Absentees' Property Law
name.ar: قانون أملاك الغائبين
name.he: חוק רכוש נפקדים

description.en: The Knesset passed the Absentees’ Property Law, vesting the property of persons defined as "absentees" (largely Palestinians who left or were displaced after 29 November 1947) in a state Custodian.
description.ar: أقرّ الكنيست قانون أملاك الغائبين الذي يضع أملاك الأشخاص المعرَّفين «غائبين» (وهم في معظمهم فلسطينيون غادروا أو هُجّروا بعد 29 تشرين الثاني/نوفمبر 1947) في عهدة قيّم حكومي.
description.he: הכנסת חוקקה את חוק נכסי נפקדים המעביר את רכושם של אנשים המוגדרים ״נפקדים״ (ברובם פלסטינים שעזבו או נעקרו אחרי 29 בנובמבר 1947) לידי אפוטרופוס ממלכתי.

sources.quote: Passed by the Knesset on the 25th Adar, 5710 (14th March 1950)
all absentees' property is hereby vested in the Custodian
The Absentees’ Property Law was the main legal instrument used by Israel to take possession of the land belonging to the internal and external Palestinian refugees

notes.en: Published in Sefer Ha-Chukkim on 20 March 1950. The law’s own framing is custodianship of absentees’ property; Adalah (legal NGO for Palestinian citizens of Israel) describes it as the main instrument used to take possession of the land of internal and external Palestinian refugees and of waqf property. An Israeli government commentary on the law was not opened. Place of passage not recorded in the sources opened.

name.en: Jordan formally unites/annexes the West Bank
name.ar: الأردن يوحّد الضفة الغربية/يضمها رسمياً
name.he: ירדן מאחדת/מספחת רשמית את הגדה המערבית

description.en: Jordan’s newly elected parliament, with equal representation of both banks, unanimously adopted an act uniting the West Bank (including East Jerusalem) with the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan.
description.ar: أقرّ البرلمان الأردني المنتخب حديثاً، بتمثيل متساوٍ للضفتين، بالإجماع قانون وحدة الضفة الغربية (بما فيها القدس الشرقية) مع المملكة الأردنية الهاشمية.
description.he: הפרלמנט הירדני שנבחר זה עתה, עם ייצוג שווה לשתי הגדות, אימץ פה אחד חוק לאיחוד הגדה המערבית (כולל מזרח ירושלים) עם הממלכה ההאשמית הירדנית.

sources.quote: an Act providing for this union was unanimously adopted on 24th April by the Jordan Assembly, which is composed of representatives of both these territories, and received the Royal Assent on the same day.
On 24 April 1950, the West Bank was brought formally under Jordanian control.

In 1950, a Jordanian parliament in which Palestinian Arabs from the West Bank were equally represented voted unanimously to unite the West Bank of the Jordan River with the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan
Egypt strongly opposed the union. Syria criticized it but did not oppose it outright.

notes.en: Terminology differs: Jordanian official sources speak of the "unity of the two banks"; others call it an annexation. Britain recognised the union but, pending a final determination of Jerusalem’s status, did not recognise Jordanian sovereignty over any part of the Jerusalem area (recognising de facto authority only), and regarded the armistice line as the frontier pending a settlement (Hansard); Egypt opposed it. Jordan renounced its claims in 1988.

name.en: Law of Return
name.ar: قانون العودة
name.he: חוק השבות

description.en: The Knesset passed the Law of Return, granting every Jew the right to immigrate to Israel as an oleh.
description.ar: أقرّ الكنيست قانون العودة الذي يمنح كل يهودي حق الهجرة إلى إسرائيل بصفة «عولِه» (مهاجر).
description.he: הכנסת חוקקה את חוק השבות המעניק לכל יהודי את הזכות לעלות לישראל כעולה.

sources.quote: Every Jew has the right to come to this country as an oleh
Passed by the Knesset on the 20th Tammuz, 5710 (5th July, 1950)
The law was meant to ensure a safe haven for a long-persecuted people in the immediate aftermath of the Holocaust
No comparable law exists to guarantee the rights of Palestinians to immigrate or receive citizenship, even if they were born in the area that is now the State of Israel.

notes.en: Facts agreed; assessments differ. Britannica summarises its purpose as a safe haven after the Holocaust and maintaining a Jewish majority; Adalah lists it among laws it considers discriminatory against Palestinians. Britannica notes a 1970 amendment extending rights to children, grandchildren and spouses of Jews (outside this record’s date). Place of passage not recorded in the sources opened.

name.en: Palestine Liberation Organization founded
name.ar: تأسيس منظمة التحرير الفلسطينية
name.he: הקמת ארגון השחרור הפלסטיני

description.en: The first Palestinian National Congress, convened in Jerusalem by Ahmad al-Shuqairi following the January 1964 Cairo Arab summit, proclaimed the Palestine Liberation Organization and adopted its National Charter and Basic Law.
description.ar: أعلن المجلس الوطني الفلسطيني الأول، الذي عقده أحمد الشقيري في القدس بعد قمة القاهرة العربية في كانون الثاني/يناير 1964، قيام منظمة التحرير الفلسطينية وأقرّ ميثاقها القومي ونظامها الأساسي.
description.he: הקונגרס הלאומי הפלסטיני הראשון, שכינס אחמד אל־שוקיירי בירושלים בעקבות ועידת הפסגה הערבית בקהיר בינואר 1964, הכריז על ארגון השחרור הפלסטיני ואימץ את האמנה הלאומית שלו ואת החוק היסודי.

sources.quote: This first congress was held in Jerusalem on 28 May 1964, under the sponsorship of King Hussein of Jordan, with nearly 400 appointed delegates attending.
On 2 June 1964, the PNC announced the creation of the PLO and approved a National Charter and a Basic Law of the organization.
The first national conference was held inJerusalem on 28May -2June 1964.

sources.locator: Part II, quoting the Israeli representative in the 1974 General Assembly debate
sources.quote: It was established at the first summit meeting of the Heads of Arab States in Cairo in 1964 as an instrument for waging terror warfare against Israel.

notes.en: Session 28 May - 2 June 1964 (end date = proclamation of the PLO). Shuqairi was elected its first chairman. The PNC website counts 422 members, palquest "nearly 400" delegates. Characterisations differ: Palestinian sources present the PLO as the representative of the Palestinian people’s liberation movement (palquest), while Israel’s UN representative in 1974 described it as a creation of the Arab governments rather than of the Palestinian community (quoted in the UN study). The 1964 charter was revised in 1968.

name.en: Israel extends its law and municipal boundaries to East Jerusalem
name.ar: إسرائيل تمدّ قانونها وحدودها البلدية إلى القدس الشرقية
name.he: ישראל מחילה את חוקיה ואת גבולותיה העירוניים על מזרח ירושלים

description.en: After the June 1967 war the Knesset authorised the government to apply Israeli law, jurisdiction and administration to designated areas, and a government order of 28 June applied them to East Jerusalem and surrounding areas, which were joined to an enlarged Jerusalem municipality.
description.ar: بعد حرب حزيران/يونيو 1967 خوّل الكنيست الحكومة تطبيق القانون والقضاء والإدارة الإسرائيلية على مناطق محددة، وطبّق أمر حكومي في 28 حزيران/يونيو ذلك على القدس الشرقية ومناطق محيطة بها ضُمّت إلى بلدية القدس الموسّعة.
description.he: לאחר מלחמת יוני 1967 הסמיכה הכנסת את הממשלה להחיל את החוק, השיפוט והמינהל הישראליים על אזורים מוגדרים, וצו ממשלתי מ־28 ביוני החיל אותם על מזרח ירושלים ועל אזורים סמוכים, שצורפו לעיריית ירושלים המורחבת.

sources.locator: para. 39 (PDF/OCR text; quote normalised for OCR, hyphenation and ligature errors)
sources.quote: Under the Law and Administration Ordinance (Amendment No. 11) Law of 27 June 1967, it was provided that the law, jurisdiction and administration of the State should apply

sources.locator: para. 39 (PDF/OCR text; quote normalised for OCR, hyphenation and ligature errors)
sources.quote: the Government issued an order dated 28 June 1967 which declared that a territory defined in an annex was an area in which the law, jurisdiction and administration of the State of Israel were in force

sources.locator: Israeli Foreign Minister's reply of 10 July 1967 (PDF/OCR text; quote normalised for OCR, hyphenation and ligature errors)
sources.quote: The term "annexation" used by supporters of the resolution is out of place. The measures adopted relate to the integration of Jerusalem in the administrative and municipal spheres
On 28 June 1967, Israel adopted legislation annexing East Jerusalem and uniting it under the authority of the city administration of West Jerusalem.

notes.en: Facts agreed; characterisation contested. Israel’s government described the measures as administrative and municipal "integration", not annexation (S/8052); Palestinian accounts (palquest) treat them as annexation; the UN General Assembly responded with resolution 2253 (ES-V) of 4 July 1967 (cited in S/8052). The annexed area included the Old City, Sur Baher, Sheikh Jarrah, Qalandia airport, Mount Scopus and Shuʿafat (S/8146 para. 39). End date = government order of 28 June.

name.en: Khartoum Arab summit resolution
name.ar: قرار قمة الخرطوم العربية
name.he: החלטת ועידת הפסגה הערבית בחרטום

description.en: An Arab League summit in Khartoum resolved to pursue the recovery of the territories occupied in June 1967 on the principles of "no peace with Israel, no recognition of Israel, no negotiations with it".
description.ar: قررت قمة لجامعة الدول العربية في الخرطوم متابعة استعادة الأراضي المحتلة في حزيران/يونيو 1967 على أساس «لا صلح مع إسرائيل، ولا اعتراف بإسرائيل، ولا مفاوضات معها».
description.he: ועידת פסגה של הליגה הערבית בחרטום החליטה לפעול להשבת השטחים שנכבשו ביוני 1967 על פי העקרונות ״לא שלום עם ישראל, לא הכרה בישראל, לא משא ומתן עמה״.

sources.quote: no peace with Israel, no recognition of Israel, no negotiations with it, and insistence on the rights of the Palestinian people in their own country.

notes.en: Single primary source (Avalon text). Interpretations of the "three noes" differ in the literature (not summarised here).

name.en: UN Security Council Resolution 242
name.ar: قرار مجلس الأمن الدولي 242
name.he: החלטת מועצת הביטחון של האו״ם 242

description.en: The UN Security Council unanimously set out principles for a peace settlement: Israeli withdrawal "from territories occupied in the recent conflict" and an end to belligerency with respect for every state’s right to live in peace within secure and recognised boundaries, plus a just settlement of the refugee problem.
description.ar: وضع مجلس الأمن الدولي بالإجماع مبادئ لتسوية سلمية: انسحاب إسرائيلي «من أراضٍ احتُلت في النزاع الأخير» وإنهاء حالة الحرب مع احترام حق كل دولة في العيش بسلام داخل حدود آمنة ومعترف بها، إضافة إلى تسوية عادلة لمشكلة اللاجئين.
description.he: מועצת הביטחון של האו״ם קבעה פה אחד עקרונות להסדר שלום: נסיגה ישראלית ״משטחים שנכבשו בסכסוך האחרון״ וסיום המצב של לוחמה תוך כיבוד זכותה של כל מדינה לחיות בשלום בתוך גבולות בטוחים ומוכרים, וכן פתרון צודק לבעיית הפליטים.

sources.locator: operative para. 1(i) (PDF/OCR text; quote normalised for OCR, hyphenation and ligature errors)
sources.quote: Withdrawal of Israel armed forces from territories occupied in the recent conflict

sources.locator: French text, para. 1(i) (accents restored) (PDF/OCR text; quote normalised for OCR, hyphenation and ligature errors)
sources.quote: Retrait des forces armées israéliennes des territoires occupés lors du récent conflit

sources.locator: adoption note (PDF/OCR text; quote normalised for OCR, hyphenation and ligature errors)
sources.quote: Adopted unanimously at the 1382nd meeting.
Arab-Soviet attempts to have the resolution demand Israel’s total withdrawal to the former armistice lines were rejected by the resolution’s sponsors
Others reject this interpretation, often pointing to the official French version of the resolution, which includes a definite article, referring to withdrawal from “des territoires.”
it did not explicitly mention Palestine; the only cognizance of the underlying issue of Palestine was in the reference to “the refugee problem”.

notes.en: Text agreed; the withdrawal clause is contested. The Israeli reading (e.g. Blum) is that the omission of "the" before "territories" was deliberate and that final boundaries are to be negotiated; Arab and Palestinian readings point to the French text ("des territoires") and to the preamble’s emphasis on "the inadmissibility of the acquisition of territory by war" (resolution text; palquest presents both views). The UN study notes the resolution treated Palestine only as a refugee problem; the PNC’s 1988 Political Communiqué accepted 242 and 338 as the basis of an international conference (pnc-declaration-1988).

name.en: UN Security Council Resolution 338
name.ar: قرار مجلس الأمن الدولي 338
name.he: החלטת מועצת הביטחון של האו״ם 338

description.en: During the October 1973 war the Security Council called for a cease-fire, implementation of Resolution 242 "in all of its parts", and negotiations between the parties "under appropriate auspices".
description.ar: دعا مجلس الأمن خلال حرب تشرين الأول/أكتوبر 1973 إلى وقف إطلاق النار وتنفيذ القرار 242 «بجميع أجزائه» وإجراء مفاوضات بين الأطراف «تحت رعاية مناسبة».
description.he: במהלך מלחמת אוקטובר 1973 קראה מועצת הביטחון להפסקת אש, ליישום החלטה 242 ״על כל חלקיה״ ולמשא ומתן בין הצדדים ״תחת חסות מתאימה״.

sources.quote: negotiations shall start between the parties concerned under appropriate auspices aimed at establishing a just and durable peace in the Middle East.

sources.locator: adoption note (PDF/OCR text; quote normalised for OCR, hyphenation and ligature errors)
sources.quote: Adopted at the 1747th meeting by 14 votes to none

notes.en: China did not participate in the vote (footnote to the text).

name.en: Rabat Arab summit recognises the PLO as sole legitimate representative
name.ar: قمة الرباط العربية تعترف بمنظمة التحرير ممثلاً شرعياً وحيداً
name.he: ועידת הפסגה הערבית ברבאט מכירה בארגון השחרור הפלסטיני כנציג הלגיטימי היחיד

description.en: The Arab heads of state meeting at Rabat affirmed the Palestinian people’s right to an independent national authority under the PLO, "the sole legitimate representative of the Palestinian people"; Jordan’s King Hussein joined the decision.
description.ar: أكد رؤساء الدول العربية المجتمعون في الرباط حق الشعب الفلسطيني في سلطة وطنية مستقلة بقيادة منظمة التحرير، «الممثل الشرعي والوحيد للشعب الفلسطيني»؛ وانضم الملك حسين ملك الأردن إلى القرار.
description.he: ראשי המדינות הערביות שהתכנסו ברבאט אישרו את זכות העם הפלסטיני לרשות לאומית עצמאית בהנהגת ארגון השחרור הפלסטיני, ״הנציג הלגיטימי היחיד של העם הפלסטיני״; המלך חוסיין מלך ירדן הצטרף להחלטה.

sources.locator: Part II, section VII, quoting the Rabat resolution
sources.quote: Affirms the right of the Palestinian people to set up an independent national authority under the leadership of the Palestinian Liberation Organization
King Hussein agreed with all the other Arab leaders to a declaration recognizing the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO) as the “sole legitimate representative of the Palestinian people.”
The seventh Arab Summit, Rabat, held in October 1974, stressed the right of the Palestinian people to return to their homeland and exercise self-determination

sources.locator: Part II, quoting the Israeli representative, November 1974
sources.quote: by the decisions adopted at the recent Rabat Conference, the Arab Governments have reaffirmed their association with the umbrella organization of the Arab murder squads

notes.en: Month precision: the exact day (commonly given as 28 October 1974) was not verified in the sources opened. The UN study stresses the significance of Jordan’s acceptance, since Jordan had administered the West Bank from 1948 to 1967; Israel’s UN representative condemned the Rabat decisions (quoted in the UN study).

name.en: Yasser Arafat addresses the UN General Assembly
name.ar: ياسر عرفات يخاطب الجمعية العامة للأمم المتحدة
name.he: יאסר ערפאת נואם בעצרת הכללית של האו״ם

description.en: PLO Executive Committee chairman Yasser Arafat addressed the UN General Assembly in the debate on the question of Palestine ("olive branch" speech); Israel’s representative replied rejecting the PLO.
description.ar: خاطب رئيس اللجنة التنفيذية لمنظمة التحرير ياسر عرفات الجمعية العامة للأمم المتحدة في مناقشة القضية الفلسطينية (خطاب «غصن الزيتون»)؛ ورد ممثل إسرائيل رافضاً منظمة التحرير.
description.he: יו״ר הוועד הפועל של ארגון השחרור הפלסטיני יאסר ערפאת נאם בעצרת הכללית של האו״ם בדיון בשאלת פלסטין (נאום ״ענף הזית״); נציג ישראל השיב ודחה את ארגון השחרור הפלסטיני.

sources.quote: On 13 November 1974, Mr. Yasser Arafat, Chairman of the Executive Committee of the PLO, addressed the General Assembly.
Today I have come bearing an olive branch and a freedom-fighter’s gun. Do not let the olive branch fall from my hand.

sources.locator: Part II, quoting the Israeli reply (A/PV.2283)
sources.quote: concerned primarily not with the realization of the rights of the Palestinians, but with the annulment of the rights of the Jewish people.

notes.en: Speech record: A/PV.2282 (not opened directly; quoted via the UN study). In October 1974 the General Assembly had invited the PLO to participate in the plenary debate on the question of Palestine (resolution 3210 (XXIX), 105 votes to 4, per the UN study).

name.en: UN General Assembly Resolutions 3236 and 3237
name.ar: قرارا الجمعية العامة للأمم المتحدة 3236 و3237
name.he: החלטות העצרת הכללית של האו״ם 3236 ו־3237

description.en: The UN General Assembly reaffirmed the inalienable rights of the Palestinian people, including self-determination, national independence and return (3236), and granted the PLO observer status (3237).
description.ar: أعادت الجمعية العامة للأمم المتحدة تأكيد الحقوق غير القابلة للتصرف للشعب الفلسطيني، ومنها تقرير المصير والاستقلال الوطني والعودة (3236)، ومنحت منظمة التحرير صفة مراقب (3237).
description.he: העצרת הכללית של האו״ם אישרה מחדש את הזכויות הבלתי ניתנות לערעור של העם הפלסטיני, ובהן ההגדרה העצמית, העצמאות הלאומית והשיבה (3236), והעניקה לארגון השחרור הפלסטיני מעמד משקיף (3237).

sources.locator: para. 1 (PDF/OCR text; quote normalised for OCR, hyphenation and ligature errors)
sources.quote: Reaffirms the inalienable rights of the Palestinian people in Palestine, including: (a) The right to self-determination without external interference

sources.locator: para. 1 (PDF/OCR text; quote normalised for OCR, hyphenation and ligature errors)
sources.quote: Invites the Palestine Liberation Organization to participate in the sessions and the work of the General Assembly in the capacity of observer

sources.locator: closing formula (PDF/OCR text; quote normalised for OCR, hyphenation and ligature errors)
sources.quote: 2296th plenary meeting 22 November 1974
Votes: 95 in favour, 17 against, 19 abstentions.
recognized the PLO as the representative of the Palestinian people and granted it observer status at the UN (Resolution 3237)

notes.en: Vote figures quoted are those the UN study gives for 3237. Israel opposed both resolutions; its representative’s position in the debate is quoted under the Arafat address record.

name.en: UN General Assembly Resolution 3379 ("Zionism is a form of racism")
name.ar: قرار الجمعية العامة للأمم المتحدة 3379 («الصهيونية شكل من أشكال العنصرية»)
name.he: החלטת העצרת הכללית של האו״ם 3379 (״הציונות היא סוג של גזענות״)

description.en: The UN General Assembly adopted a resolution determining that "zionism is a form of racism and racial discrimination"; it was revoked in 1991.
description.ar: اعتمدت الجمعية العامة للأمم المتحدة قراراً يقضي بأن «الصهيونية شكل من أشكال العنصرية والتمييز العنصري»؛ وقد أُلغي سنة 1991.
description.he: העצרת הכללית של האו״ם אימצה החלטה הקובעת ש״הציונות היא סוג של גזענות ואפליה גזעית״; היא בוטלה ב־1991.

sources.locator: operative paragraph (PDF/OCR text; quote normalised for OCR, hyphenation and ligature errors)
sources.quote: Determines that zionism is a form of racism and racial discrimination.

sources.locator: closing formula (PDF/OCR text; quote normalised for OCR, hyphenation and ligature errors)
sources.quote: 2400th plenary meeting 10 November 1975

sources.locator: US statement introducing A/46/L.47, 16 December 1991 (PDF/OCR text; quote normalised for OCR, hyphenation and ligature errors)
sources.quote: It branded the national aspirations of one people, and one people only, as illegitimate

notes.en: In 1991 the US representative introducing its revocation called it one of the Assembly’s "most ungenerous acts", while Yemen and Sudan contested the revocation procedure, arguing it required a two-thirds majority (A/46/PV.74). Revoked by resolution 46/86 on 16 December 1991 (see separate record).

name.en: Land Day general strike
name.ar: إضراب يوم الأرض العام
name.he: שביתת יום האדמה הכללית

description.en: Palestinian citizens of Israel held a general strike and demonstrations, centred in the Galilee (Sakhnin, Arraba, Deir Hanna), against government plans to expropriate Arab-owned land; protesters were killed in clashes with Israeli police and army, and the day has since been commemorated annually as Land Day.
description.ar: نفّذ المواطنون الفلسطينيون في إسرائيل إضراباً عاماً وتظاهرات، تركزت في الجليل (سخنين وعرابة ودير حنا)، ضد مخططات حكومية لمصادرة أراضٍ يملكها عرب؛ وقُتل متظاهرون في اشتباكات مع الشرطة والجيش الإسرائيليين، ويُحيا هذا اليوم سنوياً منذ ذلك الحين باسم يوم الأرض.
description.he: אזרחים פלסטינים של ישראל קיימו שביתה כללית והפגנות, שרוכזו בגליל (סח׳נין, עראבה, דיר חנא), נגד תוכניות ממשלתיות להפקיע קרקעות בבעלות ערבית; מפגינים נהרגו בהתנגשויות עם משטרת ישראל והצבא, והיום מונצח מאז מדי שנה כיום האדמה.

sources.quote: declared 30 March 1976 as a day of widespread protest in defense of the Palestinian land that Israel was threatening to confiscate for Jewish settlements.
Despite these repressive measures, the strike was total in most Arab towns and villages.

notes.en: Recorded here as a political event (strike and protest), not as a conflict; casualty figures are intentionally omitted (see palquest for names of those killed). Only a Palestinian-perspective source (palquest, Bashir) was opened; an Israeli official or press account was not found within this research session, so the Israeli government’s framing of the land measures is not documented here.

name.en: Anwar Sadat visits Jerusalem and addresses the Knesset
name.ar: أنور السادات يزور القدس ويخاطب الكنيست
name.he: אנואר סאדאת מבקר בירושלים ונואם בכנסת

description.en: Egyptian President Anwar Sadat visited Israel and addressed the Knesset in Jerusalem with a plan for a peace settlement.
description.ar: زار الرئيس المصري أنور السادات إسرائيل وخاطب الكنيست في القدس بخطة لتسوية سلمية.
description.he: נשיא מצרים אנואר סאדאת ביקר בישראל ונאם בכנסת בירושלים עם תוכנית להסדר שלום.

sources.quote: Egyptian Pres. Anwar Sadat addressing the Knesset, November 20, 1977.
In November 1977, he made a historic visit to Israel, addressing the Knesset (parliament) in Jerusalem with a plan for a peaceful settlement.
announcing on November 9 that he would be willing to go to Jerusalem. This move stunned the world.
Sadat had given up the power of a united Arab front and the recognition card, having already visited Jerusalem

notes.en: Date = Knesset address (20 November 1977); the visit spanned several days in November 1977 (exact arrival date not verified in the sources opened). The visit led to direct Egyptian-Israeli talks (Office of the Historian); Palestinian accounts (palquest, Winder) present it as Egypt giving up Arab collective leverage.

name.en: Camp David Accords
name.ar: اتفاقيتا كامب ديفيد
name.he: הסכמי קמפ דיוויד

description.en: After a summit at Camp David (5-17 September 1978) hosted by US President Jimmy Carter, Egypt’s Anwar Sadat and Israel’s Menachem Begin signed two frameworks: one for an Egyptian-Israeli peace treaty and one for a wider peace including self-government for the West Bank and Gaza.
description.ar: بعد قمة في كامب ديفيد (5-17 أيلول/سبتمبر 1978) استضافها الرئيس الأمريكي جيمي كارتر، وقّع أنور السادات من مصر ومناحيم بيغن من إسرائيل إطارين: أحدهما لمعاهدة سلام مصرية - إسرائيلية والآخر لسلام أوسع يشمل حكماً ذاتياً للضفة الغربية وغزة.
description.he: לאחר פסגה בקמפ דיוויד (5–17 בספטמבר 1978) בהנחיית נשיא ארצות הברית ג׳ימי קרטר, חתמו אנואר סאדאת ממצרים ומנחם בגין מישראל על שתי מסגרות: האחת להסכם שלום בין מצרים לישראל והאחרת לשלום רחב יותר הכולל שלטון עצמי בגדה המערבית וברצועת עזה.

sources.locator: Framework for Peace in the Middle East, opening
sources.quote: met with Jimmy Carter, President of the United States of America, at Camp David from September 5 to September 17, 1978
The Camp David Accords were agreements between Israel and Egypt, signed on September 17, 1978, following negotiations at Camp David, Maryland, brokered by U.S. President Jimmy Carter.
The Camp David Summit, held from September 5–17, 1978, was a pivotal moment both in the history of the Arab-Israeli dispute and U.S. diplomacy.
Many Arabs saw this framework for a comprehensive peace as a nonstarter. It had been negotiated without the involvement of most key actors, most prominently the PLO

notes.en: The US account stresses the summit as a diplomatic breakthrough; Palestinian accounts (palquest) note that the Palestinian autonomy framework was negotiated without the PLO and left Jerusalem unmentioned. Sadat and Begin shared the 1978 Nobel Peace Prize (Britannica, Sadat). Coordinates: Camp David (negotiation venue).

name.en: Egypt-Israel Peace Treaty
name.ar: معاهدة السلام المصرية - الإسرائيلية
name.he: הסכם השלום בין מצרים לישראל

description.en: Egypt and Israel signed a peace treaty in Washington ending the state of war; Israel undertook to withdraw its forces and civilians from the Sinai behind the international boundary of mandated Palestine.
description.ar: وقّعت مصر وإسرائيل معاهدة سلام في واشنطن أنهت حالة الحرب؛ وتعهدت إسرائيل بسحب قواتها ومدنييها من سيناء إلى ما وراء الحدود الدولية لفلسطين المنتدبة.
description.he: מצרים וישראל חתמו בוושינגטון על הסכם שלום שסיים את מצב המלחמה; ישראל התחייבה לפנות את כוחותיה ואת אזרחיה מסיני אל מעבר לגבול הבין־לאומי של פלשתינה המנדטורית.

sources.quote: Israel will withdraw all its armed forces and civilians from the Sinai behind the international boundary between Egypt and mandated Palestine
the Egyptian-Israeli Peace Treaty was formally signed on March 26.
On 26 March 1979, Sadat and Begin signed a peace treaty based on these principles in Washington, DC.
Israel concluded in 1979 a peace treaty with its southern neighbor, withdrawing in stages from the entire Sinai

notes.en: Israel withdrew from Sinai in stages to the Rafah-Taba line (Blum); the completion date (1982) was not verified in the sources opened, so no separate record is made for it.

name.en: Basic Law: Jerusalem, Capital of Israel
name.ar: القانون الأساسي: القدس عاصمة إسرائيل
name.he: חוק יסוד: ירושלים בירת ישראל

description.en: The Knesset adopted a Basic Law declaring "Jerusalem, complete and united" the capital of Israel; the UN Security Council (resolution 478, 20 August 1980) declared it null and void and called on states to withdraw diplomatic missions from the city.
description.ar: اعتمد الكنيست قانوناً أساسياً يعلن «القدس الكاملة والموحدة» عاصمة لإسرائيل؛ وأعلن مجلس الأمن الدولي (القرار 478، 20 آب/أغسطس 1980) أنه باطل ولاغٍ ودعا الدول إلى سحب بعثاتها الدبلوماسية من المدينة.
description.he: הכנסת אימצה חוק יסוד המכריז על ״ירושלים השלמה והמאוחדת״ כבירת ישראל; מועצת הביטחון של האו״ם (החלטה 478, 20 באוגוסט 1980) הכריזה עליו בטל ומבוטל וקראה למדינות לסלק את נציגויותיהן הדיפלומטיות מהעיר.

sources.quote: Adopted by the Knesset on 30 July 1980
Jerusalem, complete and united, is the capital of Israel.

sources.locator: operative para. 2 (PDF/OCR text; quote normalised for OCR, hyphenation and ligature errors)
sources.quote: Affirms that the enactment of the "basic law" by Israel constitutes a violation of international law

sources.locator: operative para. 5 (PDF/OCR text; quote normalised for OCR, hyphenation and ligature errors)
sources.quote: Decides not to recognize the "basic law"

sources.locator: operative para. 5(b) (PDF/OCR text; quote normalised for OCR, hyphenation and ligature errors)
sources.quote: Those States that have established diplomatic missions at Jerusalem to withdraw such missions from the Holy City
the establishment of an independent Palestinian state with Jerusalem as its capital

notes.en: Israel’s position is stated in the law itself; the Security Council declared it a violation of international law and null and void, and the UN study (Part III) records that 13 countries then withdrew their missions from Jerusalem. The PLO/PNC goal is a Palestinian state with Jerusalem as its capital (PNC website). The text reproduced by palquest includes Amendment no. 1 (2000), which is outside this record.

name.en: Golan Heights Law
name.ar: قانون مرتفعات الجولان
name.he: חוק רמת הגולן

description.en: The Knesset passed a law applying Israeli law, jurisdiction and administration to the Golan Heights, captured from Syria in 1967; on 17 December 1981 the UN Security Council declared the decision null and void.
description.ar: أقرّ الكنيست قانوناً يطبق القانون والقضاء والإدارة الإسرائيلية على مرتفعات الجولان التي استولت عليها من سوريا سنة 1967؛ وفي 17 كانون الأول/ديسمبر 1981 أعلن مجلس الأمن الدولي القرار باطلاً ولاغياً.
description.he: הכנסת חוקקה חוק המחיל את החוק, השיפוט והמינהל הישראליים על רמת הגולן, שנכבשה מסוריה ב־1967; ב־17 בדצמבר 1981 הכריזה מועצת הביטחון של האו״ם על ההחלטה בטלה ומבוטלת.

sources.quote: This legislation, extending Israeli law to the area of the Golan Heights was adopted by the Knesset by a majority of 63 against 21.
The Law, jurisdiction and administration of the state shall apply to the Golan Heights, as described in the Appendix.

sources.locator: operative para. 1 (PDF/OCR text; quote normalised for OCR, hyphenation and ligature errors)
sources.quote: Decides that the Israeli decision to impose its laws, jurisdiction and administration in the occupied Syrian Golan Heights is null and void and without international legal effect

sources.locator: preamble (PDF/OCR text; quote normalised for OCR, hyphenation and ligature errors)
sources.quote: Having considered the letter of 14 December 1981 from the Permanent Representative of the Syrian Arab Republic

notes.en: Dated 14 December 1981 by the Israel MFA. Israel presented it as implementing government policy on the Golan, with Prime Minister Begin citing Syrian hostility (MFA note); the Security Council, acting on Syria’s complaint, declared it null and void and demanded that Israel rescind it (resolution 497).

name.en: Israel completes its withdrawal from Sinai
name.ar: إسرائيل تكمل انسحابها من سيناء
name.he: ישראל משלימה את נסיגתה מסיני

description.en: Israel completed its withdrawal from the Sinai Peninsula and Egyptian sovereignty was re-established under the 1979 Egypt–Israel Peace Treaty.
description.ar: أكملت إسرائيل انسحابها من شبه جزيرة سيناء وأُعيدت السيادة المصرية بموجب معاهدة السلام المصرية - الإسرائيلية لسنة 1979.
description.he: ישראל השלימה את נסיגתה מחצי האי סיני והריבונות המצרית הוחזרה מכוח הסכם השלום בין מצרים לישראל מ־1979.

sources.quote: ended on April 25, 1982, when Israel completed its withdrawal from the Sinai and Egyptian sovereignty was reestablished in accordance with the 1979 Peace Treaty
Sinai Liberation Day is observed annually on 25 April, commemorating the withdrawal of Israeli forces from the Sinai Peninsula in 1982 and the restoration of Egyptian sovereignty

notes.en: Egypt commemorates the date as Sinai Liberation Day (Egyptian Streets). The Taba enclave was not part of this handover; its status was settled later (not covered by the sources cited here). The Multinational Force and Observers took over treaty verification at this time (Reagan message).

name.en: Hamas founded
name.ar: تأسيس حماس
name.he: הקמת חמאס

description.en: Leaders of the Muslim Brotherhood in Gaza, headed by Shaykh Ahmad Yasin, met at the start of the First Intifada and agreed to set up the organisation that became known as Hamas (Islamic Resistance Movement).
description.ar: اجتمع قادة الإخوان المسلمين في غزة، برئاسة الشيخ أحمد ياسين، مع بدء الانتفاضة الأولى واتفقوا على إنشاء التنظيم الذي عُرف باسم حماس (حركة المقاومة الإسلامية).
description.he: מנהיגי האחים המוסלמים ברצועת עזה, בראשות השייח׳ אחמד יאסין, נפגשו בתחילת האינתיפאדה הראשונה והסכימו להקים את הארגון שנודע בשם חמאס (תנועת ההתנגדות האסלאמית).

sources.quote: met in Gaza City on 9 December 1987 and agreed to set up the organizational framework for a group that would enable the Brotherhood to conduct jihad against the occupation
Date: 1987 - present
Hamas Covenant 1988

notes.en: Founding meeting date per palquest (Charif); Britannica gives the year 1987. Its charter (covenant) is dated 18 August 1988 (Avalon index). Assessments of Hamas differ sharply; those debates are outside this event record.

name.en: Jordan disengages from the West Bank
name.ar: الأردن يفك الارتباط بالضفة الغربية
name.he: ירדן מתנתקת מהגדה המערבית

description.en: King Hussein announced the severing of Jordan’s legal and administrative ties with the West Bank, deferring to the PLO as the sole legitimate representative of the Palestinian people.
description.ar: أعلن الملك حسين قطع الصلات القانونية والإدارية للأردن بالضفة الغربية، تاركاً الأمر لمنظمة التحرير بوصفها الممثل الشرعي والوحيد للشعب الفلسطيني.
description.he: המלך חוסיין הודיע על ניתוק הקשרים המשפטיים והמינהליים של ירדן עם הגדה המערבית, תוך הפניה לארגון השחרור הפלסטיני כנציג הלגיטימי היחיד של העם הפלסטיני.

sources.quote: full legal and administrative disengagement from the West Bank
we respect the wish of the PLO, the sole and legitimate representative of the Palestinian people, to secede from us as an independent Palestinian state.

notes.en: Address to the Nation, Amman. The speech refers to "38 years of the unity of the two banks" and to the 1974 Rabat summit resolution. Followed four months later by the PNC declaration of independence.

name.en: Palestinian Declaration of Independence
name.ar: إعلان الاستقلال الفلسطيني
name.he: הכרזת העצמאות הפלסטינית

description.en: At its 19th session in Algiers, the Palestine National Council proclaimed the State of Palestine and, in an accompanying political communiqué, accepted UN Security Council resolutions 242 and 338 as the basis for an international peace conference.
description.ar: أعلن المجلس الوطني الفلسطيني في دورته التاسعة عشرة في الجزائر قيام دولة فلسطين، وقبل في بيان سياسي مرافق قراري مجلس الأمن 242 و338 أساساً لمؤتمر دولي للسلام.
description.he: המועצה הלאומית הפלסטינית, במושבה ה־19 באלג׳יר, הכריזה על מדינת פלסטין, ובהודעה מדינית נלווית קיבלה את החלטות מועצת הביטחון 242 ו־338 כבסיס לוועידת שלום בין־לאומית.

sources.quote: held at Algiers, from 12 to 15 November 1988
The session culminated in the adoption on 15 November of two landmark documents
affirming for the first time an acceptance of Palestine’s partition

notes.en: The UN study states that it was "immediately welcomed by the international community" and that within a month almost 80 states recognised the State of Palestine. Palquest (Charif) describes it as the first PLO acceptance of the partition of Palestine; the Israeli government’s response was not documented in the sources opened here. See also UNGA 43/177.

name.en: UN General Assembly Resolution 43/177 ("Palestine" designation)
name.ar: قرار الجمعية العامة للأمم المتحدة 43/177 (تسمية «فلسطين»)
name.he: החלטת העצרת הכללית של האו״ם 43/177 (הכינוי ״פלסטין״)

description.en: Meeting in Geneva, the UN General Assembly acknowledged the PNC’s proclamation of the State of Palestine and decided that the designation "Palestine" would be used in the UN system in place of "Palestine Liberation Organization".
description.ar: أقرّت الجمعية العامة للأمم المتحدة في جنيف إعلان المجلس الوطني الفلسطيني قيام دولة فلسطين وقررت استخدام تسمية «فلسطين» في منظومة الأمم المتحدة بدلاً من «منظمة التحرير الفلسطينية».
description.he: העצרת הכללית של האו״ם, בהתכנסה בז׳נבה, הכירה בהכרזת המועצה הלאומית הפלסטינית על מדינת פלסטין והחליטה שהכינוי ״פלסטין״ ישמש במערכת האו״ם במקום ״ארגון השחרור הפלסטיני״.

sources.quote: the General Assembly decided that, effective as of 15 December 1988, the designation “Palestine” should be used in the United Nations system in place of the previously used designation “Palestine Liberation Organization”
This resolution was adopted by 104 votes in favour to 2 against, with 36 delegations abstaining.
welcomed by the majority of delegations attending the General Assembly session in Geneva

notes.en: The session was held in Geneva (UN study). The study names the United States as one of the two delegations voting against. The change was without prejudice to the observer status and functions of the PLO.

name.en: Madrid Peace Conference
name.ar: مؤتمر مدريد للسلام
name.he: ועידת מדריד לשלום

description.en: A US-Soviet co-sponsored conference in Madrid brought Israel together with Egypt, Syria, Lebanon and a joint Jordanian-Palestinian delegation, launching direct Arab-Israeli negotiations.
description.ar: جمع مؤتمر في مدريد برعاية أمريكية - سوفييتية مشتركة إسرائيل مع مصر وسوريا ولبنان ووفد أردني - فلسطيني مشترك، فأطلق مفاوضات عربية - إسرائيلية مباشرة.
description.he: ועידה במדריד בחסות משותפת של ארצות הברית וברית המועצות כינסה יחד את ישראל, מצרים, סוריה, לבנון ומשלחת ירדנית־פלסטינית משותפת, והחלה משא ומתן ישיר ערבי־ישראלי.

sources.quote: The Conference, co-chaired by Bush and Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev, was attended by Israeli, Egyptian, Syrian, and Lebanese delegations, as well as a joint Jordanian-Palestinian delegation.
The conference took place in Madrid on 30 October, under a formal US-Soviet sponsorship.
Following the launch of the Madrid Peace Conference on 30 October 1991

notes.en: Palestinian delegates sat in a joint delegation with Jordan; palquest notes it was "common knowledge" they had been appointed by and answered to the PLO.

name.en: UN General Assembly revokes Resolution 3379 (Resolution 46/86)
name.ar: الجمعية العامة للأمم المتحدة تلغي القرار 3379 (القرار 46/86)
name.he: העצרת הכללית של האו״ם מבטלת את החלטה 3379 (החלטה 46/86)

description.en: The UN General Assembly adopted a resolution revoking the determination in resolution 3379 (1975) that Zionism is a form of racism.
description.ar: اعتمدت الجمعية العامة للأمم المتحدة قراراً يلغي القرار الوارد في القرار 3379 (1975) بأن الصهيونية شكل من أشكال العنصرية.
description.he: העצרת הכללית של האו״ם אימצה החלטה המבטלת את הקביעה בהחלטה 3379 (1975) שהציונות היא סוג של גזענות.

sources.locator: header (PDF/OCR text; quote normalised for OCR, hyphenation and ligature errors)
sources.quote: Held at Headquarters, New York, on Monday, 16 December 1991

sources.locator: text of draft A/46/L.47 as read by Yemen (PDF/OCR text; quote normalised for OCR, hyphenation and ligature errors)
sources.quote: Decides to revoke the determination contained in its resolution 3379 (XXX) of 10 November 1975.
India voted in favour of the draft resolution contained in document A/46/L.47 in the hope and expectation that an obstacle in the path to peace in west Asia would be removed

notes.en: Introduced by the United States (A/46/L.47). Yemen and Sudan moved that it required a two-thirds majority. Vote totals were not legible in the OCR of the record and are not given.

name.en: Israel-PLO letters of mutual recognition
name.ar: رسائل الاعتراف المتبادل بين إسرائيل ومنظمة التحرير
name.he: מכתבי ההכרה ההדדית בין ישראל לארגון השחרור הפלסטיני

description.en: PLO chairman Yasser Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin exchanged letters: the PLO recognised Israel’s right to exist in peace and security and renounced terrorism, and Israel recognised the PLO as the representative of the Palestinian people.
description.ar: تبادل رئيس منظمة التحرير ياسر عرفات ورئيس الوزراء الإسرائيلي إسحاق رابين رسائل: اعترفت المنظمة بحق إسرائيل في الوجود بسلام وأمن ونبذت الإرهاب، واعترفت إسرائيل بالمنظمة ممثلاً للشعب الفلسطيني.
description.he: יו״ר ארגון השחרור הפלסטיני יאסר ערפאת וראש ממשלת ישראל יצחק רבין החליפו מכתבים: הארגון הכיר בזכות ישראל להתקיים בשלום ובביטחון וזנח את הטרור, וישראל הכירה בארגון כנציג העם הפלסטיני.

sources.quote: On 9–10 September, Chairman Arafat and Prime Minister Rabin exchanged letters of mutual recognition
After an exchange of letters in September 1993 affirming Israel’s right to exist and the PLO as the representative of the Palestinian people
Israel accepted the PLO as the representative of the Palestinians, and the PLO renounced terrorism and recognized Israel’s right to exist in peace.

notes.en: Letters exchanged on 9-10 September 1993 (palquest; end date 10 September). The PLO also committed to amend articles of the Palestinian National Charter denying Israel’s right to exist (palquest). The letters themselves were not opened (Israel MFA site unreachable).

name.en: Oslo I: Declaration of Principles on Interim Self-Government Arrangements
name.ar: أوسلو 1: إعلان المبادئ بشأن ترتيبات الحكم الذاتي الانتقالي
name.he: אוסלו א׳: הצהרת העקרונות על הסדרי ממשל עצמי זמני

description.en: Israel and the PLO signed in Washington the Declaration of Principles negotiated in Oslo, providing for a Palestinian interim self-government authority in the West Bank and Gaza for a transitional period of up to five years, leading to a permanent settlement based on resolutions 242 and 338.
description.ar: وقّعت إسرائيل ومنظمة التحرير في واشنطن إعلان المبادئ الذي جرى التفاوض عليه في أوسلو، وينص على سلطة حكم ذاتي فلسطينية انتقالية في الضفة الغربية وغزة لفترة انتقالية مدتها خمس سنوات على الأكثر، تؤدي إلى تسوية دائمة قائمة على القرارين 242 و338.
description.he: ישראל וארגון השחרור הפלסטיני חתמו בוושינגטון על הצהרת העקרונות שנוהלה באוסלו, הקובעת רשות ממשל עצמי פלסטינית זמנית בגדה המערבית וברצועת עזה לתקופת מעבר של עד חמש שנים, שתוביל להסדר קבע המבוסס על החלטות 242 ו־338.

sources.quote: to establish a Palestinian Interim Self-Government Authority, the elected Council, (the "Council") for the Palestinian people in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip, for a transitional period not exceeding five years
DONE at Washington, D.C., this thirteenth day of September 1993.
On September 13, 1993, Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin and Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO) Negotiator Mahmoud Abbas signed a Declaration of Principles
Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin and PLO chair Yasser Arafat attended the accord’s signing ceremony in Washington, D.C., days later on September 13
The results of the Oslo Agreement might thus be viewed as a reconfiguring of the framework for occupation rather than a step toward statehood or liberation.

notes.en: Signatories per the UN text: Shimon Peres for Israel and Mahmud Abbas for the PLO, witnessed by the United States (Warren Christopher) and the Russian Federation; the Office of the Historian page names Rabin as signatory, which differs from the document. Assessments differ: the US account presents it as the start of a peace process toward permanent-status talks, while palquest (Fischbach) argues in hindsight that it reconfigured the occupation rather than leading to statehood. Opposition on both sides is outside this record.

name.en: Paris Protocol on Israeli-Palestinian economic relations
name.ar: بروتوكول باريس بشأن العلاقات الاقتصادية الإسرائيلية - الفلسطينية
name.he: פרוטוקול פריז ליחסים הכלכליים בין ישראל לפלסטינים

description.en: Israel and the PLO signed in Paris the Protocol on Economic Relations, which set the framework for economic arrangements of the Palestinian self-government and was later incorporated into the Interim Agreement.
description.ar: وقّعت إسرائيل ومنظمة التحرير في باريس بروتوكول العلاقات الاقتصادية الذي وضع إطار الترتيبات الاقتصادية للحكم الذاتي الفلسطيني وأُدرج لاحقاً في الاتفاق المرحلي.
description.he: ישראל וארגון השחרור הפלסטיני חתמו בפריז על פרוטוקול היחסים הכלכליים שקבע את מסגרת ההסדרים הכלכליים של הממשל העצמי הפלסטיני ושולב בהמשך בהסכם הביניים.
